page: Microsoft Azure D16plds_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the DPLDSv5 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled with a 614 GB local SSD, and the instance is premium storage capable. No GPU accelerators are present on this server type.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 28883.33 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9656.0. Single-core performance is relatively weaker, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 1092.0 and a weak single-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 8.88 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is measured at 119.88 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations and 68.21 GB/sec for large-block write operations. In database and web operations, the server achieves an average of 20.65 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 17.29 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The D16plds_v5 offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads that benefit from dedicated physical cores and local SSD storage without requiring high memory density. However, the 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU represents a significant tradeoff for memory-intensive applications. Additionally, cryptographic performance is weak, with a Passmark CPU encryption score of 2592.37, and text generation on small language models is poor at 30.85 tokens per second. This server is suited for multi-threaded workloads with low memory footprints, such as static web serving, software compilation, and basic database operations.
